column1: # .github/timer-audit.tsv - every periodic tick and every credential lifetime
# in this tree, classified, each naming the fact behind it.
# principles.md: a state change follows a checkable FACT, never a clock. A
# timeout is allowed on a single I/O call. A periodic tick is allowed as a
# safety net that RE-CHECKS a fact. Every unavoidable bound needs a comment
# That rule is easy to agree with and easy to lose. Each of the bounds below was
# added for a reason that made sense where it was written; what nothing recorded
# was which KIND it is, and therefore whether the fact behind it still exists.
#   tick       a periodic construct that re-checks a fact. `fact` names it.
#   ttl        a credential lifetime. `fact` names what it is a safety net
#              over, or the word `none` - and then `cite` must say where that
#              is recorded, because a credential whose validity the clock
#              decides on its own IS clock-driven state.
#   io-bound   a bound on one I/O call, which principles.md allows outright.
#   retention  neither: a cache or data-retention bound that decides no
#              credential's validity and no state transition.
# The `fact` column is the point of the file. A row that names no fact is a

Moved here from secretstoretest's Harness.waitHealthy when the identity harness came to need the same wait (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#966, ARCH-DRY). The tick only re-asks the check; the wait ends on the awaited answer, on the process exiting (or a check's Final error, for a container), or on the caller's ctx (recheckInterval's comment).

column7: The tick only re-checks the live path after the store was sent SIGHUP; the wait ends on the new inode. Expiry of ReopenWait (30s) rolls the rename back, so the store is never left writing to a copy because a timer fired.

column5: sys/health answers 200 initialized and unsealed after a caller started the store: the seal rotation after each restart (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#830), the backup after its cold copy (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#765), the OS update's pre-update copy after its cold copy (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#800), and a control plane's update of itself after its reboot, before the commit (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#767)
column7: The tick only re-asks the store after a start; the wait ends on the 200. Each caller's bound (UnsealWait, 30s) never carries it on: the rotation rolls back to Clean or stops with the seal files as they are, raising the incomplete-rotation alert; the backup fails its step and releases its quiesce, so the store's real readiness alert shows; the pre-update copy refuses the update before install, keeps the previous copy, and releases its quiesce the same way. The self-update's bound is instead the self-update window (selfUpdateWindow, 5 min, or the step's deadline when sooner); when it runs out the update goes to mark-bad, never to a commit.
